item.research_question: How can a Co-Cr-Ni-based medium-entropy alloy be designed to achieve simultaneous ultra-high strength and sufficient uniform ductility by controlling composition, thermomechanical processing, and microstructural features?
item.material_system: Co34.46Cr32.12Ni27.42Al3Ti3 (in at%) medium-entropy alloy with FCC matrix and L12 precipitates
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting, homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h, hot-rolling at 1100 °C (50% reduction), cryo-rolling (CR) at 77 K to 80% total reduction, high-temperature annealing at 900 °C for 1 h (CRA), and subsequent aging at 700 °C for 4 h (CRAA)
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile testing at ambient temperature with a constant strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
key_findings: Achieved ultimate tensile strength (σu) of 2.2 GPa and uniform elongation (εue) of 13% in the CRAA-treated alloy.
The dual heterogeneous structure consists of a matrix with coarse grains (10–30 μm) and ultra-fine grains (0.5–2 μm).
Heterogeneous L12 nanoprecipitates range from several to hundreds of nanometers with a total volume fraction of 24.2%.
The lattice mismatch between the FCC matrix and L12 precipitates is extremely low at 0.011%.
The average size of fine L12 precipitates is 4.14 ± 0.62 nm with a number density of 3.4 × 1024 m−3.
Strengthening contributions calculated as: solid-solution (49 MPa), HDI hardening (800 MPa), and precipitation hardening (1115 MPa).
No twins or hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phase formed after deformation up to ~2.0 GPa stress.
Dislocation density in the fractured sample reached 3.83 × 1014 m−2 due to Lomer–Cottrell locks.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the superior properties to a combination of HDI strengthening from the heterogeneous grain structure, precipitation hardening from high-density coherent L12 particles, and enhanced ductility from the low elastic misfit strain of the interfaces which relieves stress concentration and prevents premature fracture, while the preservation of stacking faults and high dislocation density provides significant work-hardening.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors state that the strategy opens a new avenue for the development of promising heavy-duty structural materials and that the alloy elements and treatments can be readily accepted by industry.
quotes: a Co-Cr-Ni-based medium-entropy alloy (MEA) with a dual heterogeneous structure of both matrix and precipitates can be designed to provide an ultra-high tensile strength of 2.2 GPa and uniform elongation of 13%

The heterogeneous L12 nanoprecipitates are fully coherent with the matrix, minimizing the elastic misfit strain of interfaces, relieving the stress concentration during deformation, and playing an active role in enhanced ductility.
The total yield strength estimated by Eq. (1) would be 2182 MPa, in reasonable agreement with the measured 2000 MPa.
